subject: Clarify: how long-context calls are metered + exception request
messages:
From: Alex Wojcik <alex.wojcik@brightcart.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@brightcart.com>, Dan Park <dan.park@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing question — very long context / multi-doc retrieval

Hi Olga,

Quick question from our engineering team as we evaluate Redwood for BrightCart's Product Search: our pipeline does a single request that stitches ~30 product documents (avg 5k tokens each) into a long context, then runs retrieval-augmented generation. We want to understand exactly how those bytes are billed.

Specifically:
- Do you meter per-token across the entire concatenated prompt + model output, or do you apply any session-level aggregation/ceilings?
- Is there a minimum per-call unit (e.g., 1k token minimum) or do you bill precisely by token with fractional rounding rules?
- If we use prefix caching / repeated product metadata, is there any credit or prefix reuse that lowers billable tokens?

Laura (cc'd) suggested sharing a sample invoice and the spreadsheet with projected monthly usage — attaching the rough numbers. Can Redwood offer any flexibility on the minimums while we ramp? Our total monthly token estimate is low initially (~1.1M tokens) but single-call sizes are large, and we want to avoid unexpected invoices.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Wojcik
Director of Engineering, BrightCart
attachments: pricing_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample_requests.json (attached separately)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wojcik <alex.wojcik@brightcart.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question — very long context / multi-doc retrieval

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear examples and the spreadsheet. I dug into the numbers with the pricing team; below is a concise practical answer plus a short proposal for ramp-related concessions.

How billing works (practical):
- Metering: we bill per billable token = model input tokens + model output tokens. There is no hidden per-call flat fee.
- Rounding/minimums: tokens are aggregated into a per-customer rolling window (30 days) for invoicing granularity. We do not impose a per-request 1k hard minimum; instead we apply a token quantum for low-volume smoothing. Practically, small spikes are absorbed by a monthly smoothing floor of 1,000 tokens per API call for the purposes of token quantum rounding — but that only affects invoices where total monthly volume is extremely low. For your projected 1.1M tokens/month this quantum will be immaterial for the aggregate dollars.
- Long-context handling: the runtime charges for the actual input tokenized length. If you concatenate 30 documents, tokens are counted for the full prompt you send. We do offer prefix/KV cache credits when the same exact byte-prefix is reused across calls within the same session; this reduces billable inputs when you rely on warm caches or repeated embeddings/prefix reuse.

Example from your sheet (rough):
- Single request with 30*5k tokens = ~150k input tokens + 1k output = 151k tokens.
- If you do 10 such requests/day -> ~1.51M tokens/month.
- Rounding quantum: each API call rounded up to nearest token (no fractional token billing). The 1,000-token smoothing floor would not materially change the month total at your scale.

Proposal for BrightCart while you ramp:
- We can waive the smoothing floor for the first 60 days so your per-call pattern (big single-call sizes) bills exactly per-token with no per-call minimum applied.
- Additionally, if BRG-4521 reaches >3M tokens/month within 3 months we can offer a 10% token discount on overage beyond 3M for the following quarter (standard tiered concession).

I attached a short pricing_calc.xlsx with both the base math and the waived-floor scenario under tab "BRG-4251-proj".

Next steps:
1) Rishi — can you confirm whether the waived-floor concession needs legal/finance approval or if we can approve it from pricing?
2) Alex — if that looks reasonable I can formalize the concession and send a DocuSign for signature.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing_calc.xlsx, sample_invoice.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 14:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question — very long context / multi-doc retrieval

O+L — quick internal note on approvals.

- Waived smoothing-floor for 60 days: pricing can approve up to 90 days as a standard play; finance just needs a note in the deal record. I'll add a line item in HubSpot and tag the concession. No legal redline required for a temporary billing mechanic waiver.
- Discount trigger (>3M tokens/month -> 10% overage discount): that concession is in typical sales playbook; we can approve but need the account exec to mark the ARR trigger and pre-approve renewal language. Laura — can you add the discount clause to the proposal template and confirm renewal cadence?

Also: we should document the cache-credit behavior precisely: prefix/KV cache credit only applies to byte-identical prefixes served from the same model instance pool; cross-region or switched-model calls will not automatically credit. Ops needs to know BrightCart will use a single region for best effect.

I will create the HubSpot concession record and attach the pricing_calc.xlsx. Olga please go ahead and draft the DocuSign with: waived-floor for first 60 days, 10% overage discount above 3M tokens/month for the next quarter if hit.

-Rishi

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@brightcart.com>, Dan Park <dan.park@brightcart.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing question — very long context / multi-doc retrieval

Hi Alex — following up with the agreed approach. Summary and next steps below.

Summary for BrightCart (concise):
- Metering: per-token (input + output). Large concatenated prompts are billed for the full tokenized length you send.
- Rounding: per-token, no fractional tokens; 30-day rolling aggregation for invoices.
- Smoothing-floor: waived for first 60 days for BRG-4521 (no per-call minimums applied during trial).
- Prefix/KV cache: eligible for credit when identical prefixes are reused in-session on the same model pool. We recommend using a single region for production to maximize cache reuse.
- Concession: 10% token discount on any overage above 3M tokens/month, applicable the following quarter once the threshold is met.

Action items:
1) Alex: confirm you accept the waived-floor + discount trigger. Reply to this thread and we will send the concession addendum.
2) BrightCart: confirm preferred region (us-west-2 / us-east-1) so we can lock routing and advise on cache affinity.
3) Rishi/Laura: I'll prepare the DocuSign and HubSpot concession record (attached link).

If you want the math in a different format I can export a sample invoice showing the two scenarios (with/without waived-floor). Once Alex confirms I'll route the DocuSign.

Best,
Olga Petrov
